subject: Food Science
title: History of Adulteration
description: A fast breakdown of History of Adulteration for builders.

hook.text: Victorian bakers added alum and chalk to bread. Tea merchants bulked leaves with iron filings.

buildup.text: Before regulation, food fraud was rampant. Milk was diluted; candy was colored with toxic lead salts.

discovery.text: Frederick Accum published 'There is Death in the Pot' in 1820—the first exposé of food adulteration.

twist.text: His book was so controversial that industry enemies framed him for library theft. He fled England.

climax.text: Public outrage eventually led to the UK's first Food Adulteration Act in 1860—the start of food law.

punchline.text: The first food safety whistleblower was exiled. The truth was too profitable to allow.

quiz.question: Who wrote the first major exposé of food adulteration?
